newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Profit-taking brings Hungary BUX index down 1.54pct. [CORRECTED 16:58 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking brings Hungary BUX index down 1.54pct. [CORRECTED 16:58 GMT]

text.p: A four-day bull run of the Budapest Stock Exchange ended on Friday as investors' profit-taking turned to be a healthy correction rather than a wave of panic sales traders feared in early trading.
The BUX index finished at 5,032.86 points (BSE corrects from 5,047.60), down 93.53 (corrects from 78.79) or 1.54 percent.

"Many began to take profits," said Kalman Schuszter of New York Broker Budapest. "This (profit-taking) seemed to much worse at the beginning of the day...with prices (in dollar) of Hungarian stocks began to plunge in London."
"Seeing prices in London everybody expected a heavy fall here," Schuszter said.
But good supply at lower price levels triggered new purchases which pushed prices up from the day's low but leaving still below Thursday's closing levels, traders said.
"Today's fall was a warning sign," Schuszter said, adding that sideways movements should be the logical following. "I expect the market to consolidate at these levels."
Schuszter pointed to the fact that major securities houses went ahead to unload their stocks, while domestic small investors were able to limit the price fall.
OTP Bank, which surged to a record level on Thursday, led losers in early trading by plummeting ten percent which later moderated. Finally the paper to finish seven percent lower at 3,720 forints.
Chemicals firm TVK stocks had enormous turnover of almost 500,000 stocks changing hadns. TVK closed at 2,355 forints, down 65, well above the day's low of 2,250.
Oil and gas company MOL shares were also heavily traded. After trading between a 2,450 and 2,600 forints, it closed at 2,580, down 70.
Trading was suspended for the whole session in frozen food manufacturer Goldsun shares for the whole session following newspaper reports of large losses in 1996.

"On January 17, 1997, Napi Gazdasag (newspaper) published a story titled 'Goldsun: Gigantic losses', which informed readers that...Goldsun Rt's 1996 losses approached 850 million losses...," the BSE's statement said.
The company has not confirmed the information publicly, thus the BSE has suspended trading in Goldsun in accordance with its regulation.
